eyebrow: Where the laser has to land (NIST)
caption: A micrograph of a real NIST ion trap chip, with the red dot marking exactly where a single trapped ion hovers above the gold electrodes — the target a control laser has to hit without disturbing its neighbors.

steps.label: Raman transition
steps.sub: A pair of lasers drives the rotation; pulse length and intensity set how much

steps.label: Individual addressing
steps.sub: Ions sit only micrometers apart — aiming without hitting neighbors is real optics work

steps.label: No dedicated wire
steps.sub: Unlike a superconducting qubit, there's no physical line per ion here

steps.label: Motional modes (phonons)
steps.sub: Coulomb-coupled ions share vibrational patterns across the whole chain

steps.label: Mølmer–Sørensen gate
steps.sub: Detuned lasers briefly couple two ions' states to a shared motional mode

steps.label: Gate speed tradeoff
steps.sub: Microseconds to hundreds of microseconds — roughly 2-3 orders of magnitude slower than superconducting gates

subtitle: The architecture's single biggest selling point — and where it stops being true.
